data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A large service with high internal redundancy is more resilient because it can implement complex, global load-balancing and failover strategies that small, independent services cannot coordinate.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The failure is caused by a logic error in the global load balancer itself.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The internal redundancy is 'shallow' (e.g., mirrored hardware but identical software versions).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The central operator can detect anomalies in real-time across the entire fleet and shift traffic away from failing nodes faster than independent operators can react, effectively 'outrunning' the correlation of the failure via high-bandwidth internal telemetry.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
